summary: Two-layer liveness protection: supervised-run enforces hard deadlines for killable subprocesses, while z-execute/z-overnight schedule one-shot hang-checks based on metrics-derived thresholds to detect and notify on native-agent stalls.

entry_points.summary: Schedules schedule-hang-check.sh after successful registry registration when watchdog and registry are enabled.
Schedules a one-shot hang-check at a metrics-derived horizon; no daemon teardown required.
Hard-deadline wrapper for external commands; emits dispatch leases and watchdog_timeout on enforced deadline.
Computes per-class threshold seconds from historical wall_ms p90/p95 times margin; sparse fallback to watchdog.stale_secs.
Schedules self-removing launchd one-shot or detached fallback for hang-check.sh.
One-shot liveness check; exits 0; notifies once when stale unmatched starts remain.
Read-only unmatched *_start inspector with stale threshold and lifecycle deny-list.
Best-effort Discord/macOS alert path for watchdog_stall and watchdog_timeout.
Resolve timeout, gtimeout, or bash_fallback backend.
Legacy pid-file cleanup during deregister; best-effort and non-fatal.
External reviewer provider calls are wrapped in supervised-run.
rsync/cargo/ssh remote operations run under supervised-run and emit orphan hints on timeout.

invariants: Killable subprocesses can be killed; native Agent stalls are alert-only.
dispatch_id is mandatory for robust lease matching.
supervised-run diagnostics are stderr-only; child stdout is preserved.
Exit 124 means the wrapper enforced timeout.
Scheduled hang-check exits 0 and never fails loudly.
Notify-once marker dedups repeated stall alerts.
gotchas: Old watchdog-sweep/watchdog-spawn daemon path is retired and scripts may be absent.
Notifications must be configured or stalls are silent aside from events/output.
liveness.sh lifecycle deny-list avoids treating run/phase starts as stuck subagents.
Sparse metrics classes use watchdog.stale_secs fallback.
Remote timeouts may leave remote units alive; remote-runner emits cleanup hints.

memories.text: runtime/watchdog registry: flock-on-write (atomic_write_json) serializes writes only, not read-modify-write cycles. fanout.run_fanout (fanout.py:296-309) does read_registry->mutate->write_registry unlocked; a concurrent daemon poll pass can interleave after the read and lose freshly-added child records. Serialize the full cycle (hold the registry .lock sidecar across RMW, or take the daemon single-instance lock non-blocking + retry).
